newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.

text.p: Long bond yields edged slightly weaker at the close on Monday after languishing in a narrow range for much of what dealers described as a mediocre trading day.
At the 1400 GMT finish, the key R150 was pegged at a 15.30 percent yield after trading between a low of 15.24 percent and a 15.28 percent high for all but the last hour of trade.
The benchmark gilt finished Friday at 15.27 percent.

Dealers said interest on the day was restricted by the fact that the market lacked any form of direction coupled with the fact that U.S. players were absent from the market as they celebrated the Columbus Day holiday.
"There has been a complete lack of interest in the market and a complete lack of direction and we have just drifted higher," one trader said.

Dealers said the market's move to its lower 15.24 percent level was met by "decent foreign selling". Some traders had initially expected that a breach of the 15.27 percent level on the downside would herald a renewed bull run.
"(The) 15.24 level is turning out to be quite a big resistance level. We saw some good foreign selling down there," one trader said.
Another dealer said that at the higher levels, there had also been some "good institutional interest", indicating that the market was preparing for a sharp downward move.
But with little on the local front to offer direction this week, traders said they expected the market to range-trade.
On the currency market activity was equally muted as the rand moved in a tight 4.5350 bid to 4.5435 bid range.
Dealers said the currency was helped lower early in the day by exporter dollar selling, only to be met by what appeared to be importer demand for the U.S. currency.
Volumes on the day were described as moderate.
The rand managed to regain some of its lost composure against the resurgent British pound after earlier falling to yet another record low.
At the close, the rand was pegged at 7.1647/1772 against sterling after earlier hitting a worst ever 7.1885 against the British currency.
Sterling has gained ground against the dollar, mark and yen since last week amid growing views that the British economy is gaining strength.
Against the mark, the rand was last at 0.3364/3370 from 0.3367/3373 at Friday's finish.

On the money market, three-month NCDs ticked up to between 15.80 and 16.00 percent from 15.75 to 15.95 percent on Friday, while 90-day BAs were also a touch higher at between 15.25 and 15.40 from 15.20 to 15.40 percent previously.
The daily shortage was quoted at 8.103 billion rand on Saturday from 8.108 billion rand on Friday.
Bond Exchange figures show foreigners bought a net 99.69 million rand of South African bonds on Friday after selling 87.16 million rand on Thursday.
Nominal cumulative volumes on the bond market amounted to 5.16 billion rand on Friday from 35.82 billion rand on Thursday, a settlement date.
-- Paul Richardson, Johannesburg newsroom, +27 11 482-1003
